description: Directive regulating alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) managing or marketing AIFs in the EU. Covers: authorisation, capital requirements, leverage limits, depositary requirements, investor reporting, and third-country rules.

Amending directive expanding AIFMD: loan originating funds regulation, enhanced delegation and supervisory cooperation provisions, liquidity management tools, and data reporting improvements. In force 2024, transposition by 2026.

canonical_name: UCITS — Directive 2009/65/EC (Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities)
description: Harmonised framework for UCITS funds marketed to retail investors across the EU. Establishes investment restrictions, diversification rules, fund structure, depositary requirements, and UCITS passport for cross-border distribution.

Requires manufacturers of packaged retail investment and insurance-based products (PRIIPs) to produce a Key Information Document (KID) before retail investors can invest. Funds, structured products, unit-linked insurance in scope.

Any collective investment undertaking that raises capital from investors to invest according to a defined policy for the benefit of those investors, and is not a UCITS. Includes hedge funds, private equity funds, real estate funds, and infrastructure funds.

Legal person whose regular business is managing one or more AIFs. Subject to AIFMD authorisation requirements. Must comply with conduct of business, conflict of interest, risk management, and reporting obligations.
Company authorised to manage UCITS funds. Subject to capital requirements, conduct of business rules, and host state AML requirements. UCITS ManCo passport allows cross-border management across EU.

Entity responsible for safekeeping assets and oversight of a fund manager. For UCITS: a credit institution or designated investment firm. For AIFs: additional entity types possible. Depositary has AML obligations as a financial institution and must verify BO of counterparties.

Standardised pre-contractual disclosure document for UCITS. Must be provided to retail investors before investment. Contains: fund objectives, risk and reward profile, charges, past performance. Being replaced by PRIIPs KID for UCITS.

Distributors of investment funds (AIFs and UCITS) are obliged entities under AMLR when they provide investment services. Must apply CDD to their clients. Fund manager may rely on distributor's CDD under third-party reliance arrangements (AMLR Art. 28).

AML risk: funds distributed through nominee or omnibus accounts can obscure ultimate beneficial owner. AMLR requires look-through of nominee/omnibus structures to identify underlying investors. Particularly relevant for offshore distributed funds.

AIFs domiciled in offshore jurisdictions (Cayman Islands, BVI, Luxembourg, Ireland) present elevated AML risk due to: complex ownership structures, limited BO transparency, potential use for tax evasion or ML. EDD may be required for offshore fund investments.

Type of AIF investing in private companies. Higher AML risk than public market funds due to: fewer regulatory requirements on portfolio companies, complex ownership structures, less liquid investments, potential for valuation manipulation.

AIFMD requires AIFMs to set maximum leverage levels and report leverage to competent authorities. Excessive leverage in AIFs can create systemic risk. AML: high leverage can be used to amplify position sizes and obscure economic purpose.

AIFMs and UCITS management companies are financial institutions subject to AMLR as obliged entities. CDD applies to investors in funds. Look-through obligations for nominee/omnibus structures. Fund distributors separately subject to AMLR. BO transparency obligations in fund structures.

AIFMs and UCITS management companies must comply with SFDR (Regulation 2019/2088) sustainability disclosure requirements. Article 6, 8, and 9 fund classifications require disclosure of sustainability risks and impacts. ESG risk assessment feeds into AML holistic risk picture.

Distribution of UCITS to retail investors is subject to MiFID II conduct of business rules (suitability, appropriateness, best execution). UCITS passport allows distribution across EU without separate authorisation. MiFID II distributor is an obliged entity under AMLR.

ESMA issues technical standards and guidelines on AIFMD and UCITS. Maintains central registers of authorised AIFMs and UCITS management companies. Coordinates national supervisors on cross-border fund issues. Issues guidance on AML in investment management.

CDD process for fund managers as obliged entities: (1) Identify and verify investor identity; (2) Look through nominees/omnibus accounts to underlying investors; (3) Identify BO of investing entities; (4) Screen against PEP and sanctions lists; (5) EDD for high-risk investors; (6) Ongoing monitoring of subscriptions/redemptions.

ELTIF Regulation (EU) 2015/760 as reformed by ELTIF 2.0 (2023/606). Designed for long-term investments in real economy assets, now accessible to retail investors. AML considerations: less liquid assets, complex structures, wider investor base.
